summary.text: Roger Goodman is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives from District 45-Position 1, where he has served since 2007, and he is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot seeking re-election.
An attorney and criminal justice policy consultant, he previously worked on Capitol Hill as a congressional legislative director and chief of staff.

paragraphs.text: Roger Goodman holds an A.B. from Dartmouth College (1983), a J.D. from The George Washington University (1986) and a Master of Public Administration from Harvard's Kennedy School of Government (1998).
He worked as an attorney at Tillinghast, Collins & Graham in Providence from 1986 to 1988 and on the legal staff of the Democratic National Committee in 1988.
He then served as legislative director and counsel to U.S. Representative Bob Wise from 1989 to 1993 and as chief of staff to U.S. Representative Rick Boucher from 1993 to 1995.

Goodman was executive director of the Washington State Sentencing Guidelines Commission from 1998 to 2000 and a criminal justice policy consultant to the King County Bar Association from 2000 to 2009.
He practices as an attorney licensed in state and federal courts.
He lives in Kirkland with his daughter and son.
Goodman took office in the Washington House in 2007.

Ballotpedia lists his 2023-2024 committee assignments as the Civil Rights & Judiciary Committee, the Community Safety, Justice, & Reentry Committee and the Human Services, Youth, & Early Learning Committee, and he chaired the Public Safety Committee in 2019-2020 and 2021-2022.
